body.estimand_functional: \(\theta(P)=\theta_b(P_O)\text{ for }P\in\mathcal M_b,\ b\in\{\mathrm{PT},\mathrm{SC}\}\). At a strict-interior constant-rank \(P_0\in\mathcal M_I\) satisfying \(p_X(x)>\kappa_0\), \(p_g(x)\in(\epsilon_0,1-\epsilon_0)\), strict fourth-moment and SC-spectrum margins, nonzero \(\Omega_x\)-eigenvalues greater than \(\kappa_0\), and locally constant \(\operatorname{rank}(\Omega_x)\), \(\phi_U(P_0)=\chi_0+\sum_x\{g^{\circ}_{\mathrm{PT},x}+R_{\mathrm{PT},x}^{\prime}a_x^U\}=\chi_0+\sum_x\{g^{\circ}_{\mathrm{SC},x}+R_{\mathrm{SC},x}^{\prime}d_x^U\}\), where the centered coefficients solve \(\mathrm{QP}_x\).

sampling_model.design: Independent sampling from a fixed-length micro panel with finite group and covariate supports.
sampling_model.treatment: Group one is untreated through \(T-1\) and treated only in period \(T\); every donor group remains untreated.
sampling_model.overlap: The model classes retain their displayed weak margins. The tangent, envelope, adaptation, and endpoint theorems are evaluated only at intersection laws with strict cell-mass and two-sided conditional-group-probability slack, strict fourth-moment and SC-spectrum slack, nonzero normal eigenvalues strictly above the displayed gap, and locally constant rank.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The treated-stratum probabilities \(\nu_x\), conditional contrasts \(C_b(x)\), centered gradients \(g^{\circ}_{b,x}\), normalized restriction gradients, and covariance Grams are finite-dimensional observed-law objects for strict-interior lower-bound and adaptation calculations. Sun, Xie, and Zhang's one integrated estimator has alternative PT and SC asymptotic representations. This paper proves no cross-fitted projection estimator, variance estimator, data-driven chart coupling, or multiplier procedure valid over the frozen local-sequence class.

body.tldr: Short-panel ATT identification is valid on the union of conditional parallel trends and a full-rank group-level synthetic-control mean restriction. At strict-interior, locally constant-rank intersection points, the corrected derivative separates the common treated-composition gradient \(\chi_0\) from conditionally centered stratum gradients. Their affine-class intersection and union convolution lower bound are computed by finite covariance-weighted programs, with \(E[\chi_0^2]\) added to the envelope and both oracle variances; observable Gram discrepancies characterize simultaneous and one-sided adaptation. The exact strict three-group witness and the single-donor and saturated-donor endpoints remain valid on this repaired scope. Sun, Xie, and Zhang analyze one integrated ATT estimator and one multiplier-bootstrap construction under alternative PT and SC hypotheses, with branch-specific influence functions and variances. This paper adds a sharp local lower-bound benchmark, not implemented inference; finite-coordinate splicing makes the requested uniform attainment theorem false over the frozen sequence class.

project_justification.gap: SunXieZhang2025 identifies the ATT under alternative PT and SC hypotheses and analyzes one integrated estimator and one multiplier-bootstrap construction: Theorems 2 and 3 give branch-specific influence functions and asymptotic variances that may differ, and Theorem 4 proves bootstrap consistency under either theorem's assumptions. ChenSantAnnaXie2025 derives PT efficiency alone. Neither source determines the common regular influence class or union convolution bound at strict-interior constant-rank PT--SC intersection points.
project_justification.niche: Finite covariate support turns each branch into finitely many conditional-mean restrictions. At strict-interior constant-rank theorem points, separating \(\chi_b\) from \(g^{\circ}_{b,x}\) restores the product rule; the common \(\chi_0\) is orthogonal to the centered restriction geometry, so the local efficiency loss and adaptation frontier are computable from observed conditional covariance Grams.
project_justification.fill: The project derives corrected PT and SC affine influence classes at strict-interior locally constant-rank intersection points, solves their centered intersection by stratum covariance-weighted quadratic programs, and adds \(E[\chi_0^2]\) to the union and oracle variances. It proves simultaneous and one-sided oracle criteria, the strict three-group region, and both endpoint reductions. The lower-bound and impossibility conclusions apply to estimators regular on the broader published union by restriction to this subclass, while sharpness is local to the repaired subclass. No implemented standard error or uniform multiplier theorem is delivered.

body.related_work: SunXieZhang2025 is the identification anchor and analyzes one integrated ATT estimator and one multiplier-bootstrap construction under alternative assumptions. Its PT condition is the donor-by-donor conditional final-change equality. Its SC hypothesis uses covariate-indexed weights common across periods, summing to one with negative weights allowed and \(T\ge J\); the intercept row of \(B\) encodes the sum constraint. Its identification theorem need not identify weights uniquely, while its SC estimation theorem assumes a uniformly nonsingular reference-donor difference system equivalent, after reparameterization, to full column rank of augmented \(B\). Theorems 2 and 3 give the PT and SC asymptotic laws for the integrated estimator, with influence functions and variances that may differ, and Theorem 4 gives multiplier-bootstrap consistency under either theorem's assumptions. The present model is a finite-support, uniform-margin, full-rank subclass, and the new sharpness claim is local to strict-interior constant-rank points in that subclass. ChenSantAnnaXie2025 supplies covariance-optimal PT weighting but not the nonnested union geometry. TchetgenTchetgenRobinsRotnitzky2010 studies a different union model. SantAnnaZhao2020, Proposition 1(a), equation (2.11), supplies the panel-DiD influence function, and equation (2.12) supplies its efficiency bound; equation (2.13) is for repeated cross-sections. Newey1990, Sections 2--3, supports the generic regular-estimator efficiency lower bound, while Newey1994 is retained only for its separately verified constant-rank role. NeweyRobins2018, ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2016, and DukesVansteelandtWhitney2024 are guidance for a possible repaired uniform theorem. Lower-bound and impossibility conclusions transfer by restriction to estimators regular over the broader published union; RummoEtAl2026 and the Alaska analysis in SunXieZhang2025 receive a benchmark, not a new standard-error procedure.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The corrected union envelope is a local regularity lower bound only at strict-interior intersection laws with locally constant rank and strict support, moment, SC-spectrum, and nonzero-normal-spectrum slack. Its common treated-composition component is identified analytically, but no attaining estimator, usable standard error, or multiplier-confidence procedure is established. The negative theorem uses a witness with strict slack, including in the local-score variance margin, and depends on the frozen sequence class's closure under arbitrary finite-coordinate replacements. It does not settle a redesigned common neighborhood with common QMD-score and remainder bounds. Boundary overlap, saturated moment inequalities, rank changes, covariance degeneracy, and weight restrictions require different local experiments.
body.honest_scope: The proved deliverables are strict-interior, locally constant-rank versions of the corrected tangent-normal characterization \(\mathcal I_b=\chi_b+\sum_xg^{\circ}_{b,x}+\operatorname{span}R_b\), the finite centered union convolution lower bound with \(E[\chi_0^2]\), observable oracle-adaptation tests, the exact strict three-group witness, and the single-donor and saturated-donor reductions. Sun, Xie, and Zhang supply one integrated estimator and one multiplier construction analyzed under alternative PT and SC hypotheses; this paper preserves that integrated-construction description and provides no new implemented inference. Lower-bound and impossibility conclusions transfer to estimators regular on the broader published union by restriction to the repaired subclass, while sharpness remains local to that subclass. The frozen sequence class makes a uniformly chartwise expansion false by finite-coordinate splicing, and no positive sequencewise continuation theorem is claimed.
body.interpretation: At a strict-interior constant-rank intersection law, the cost of requiring regularity under either identifying restriction is the squared-distance cost of forcing the PT and SC affine influence faces to agree. The common treated-composition term does not affect that distance but does contribute \(E[\chi_0^2]\) to every variance. A zero Gram discrepancy means local robustness is free in the specified direction; a positive discrepancy is a local efficiency cost, not an estimated diagnostic with its own sampling theory.
